column1: # deferral-watchlist.tsv — machine-checkable "not now, revisit when X" decisions (issue #432).
# Every deferral with a falsifiable revisit condition gets a row here; the
# founding incidents were two triggers that FIRED silently (the gh >= 2.94.0
# dependency-edge gate sat satisfied and unnoticed for ~3 weeks; the open-loop
# ledger's crontab-rot trigger sat fired for 37 days). deferral-watch.sh runs
# every active row's trigger_check; harness-doctor section 27 surfaces fired
# and broken entries as WARNs every week.
# Columns (TAB-separated; NO literal tabs inside a field; prose LAST so a
# plain `read` absorbs the remainder into the final field):
#   id  status  added  resolved  source  trigger_check  trigger_prose
# status: active | resolved. NEVER delete a row — resolving keeps history:
#   set status=resolved and fill the resolved date.
# trigger_check exit contract: 0 = FIRED (revisit condition is true),
#   1 = quiet, anything else = BROKEN (check cannot verify; fails closed).
#   Non-commandable triggers use "MANUAL: <why>" and are listed, never run.
arena-crontab-rot
column6: raw=$(LC_ALL=C crontab -l 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then user=$(id -un) || exit 3; [ "$rc" -eq 1 ] && [ "$raw" = "no crontab for $user" ] && exit 1; exit 3; fi; stale=0; for d in $(printf '%s\n' "$raw" | grep -o "ARENA_SEASON_END=[^ ]*" | cut -d= -f2); do [ "$(date -d "$d" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -lt "$(date +%s)" ] && stale=1; done; [ "$stale" = 1 ]
column7: Open-loop-ledger trigger: a crontab line still carries ARENA_SEASON_END past its own date (37 days stale when found 2026-08-21). Every occurrence is checked (duplicate keys included — inward-vet finding); fires if ANY is past or unparseable, quiet when all lines are removed or future-dated. A failed crontab read is broken, not empty; only exit 1 with the exact C-locale "no crontab for <current user>" diagnostic is known absence and quiet.

column1: circuit-breaker-revisit
column7: Circuit-breaker gates (monitoring that changes what agents may do) were deferred by operator direction. Fires when claude-loop.sh has real runs (~/.claude/loop-logs non-empty), i.e. the nightly loop is live and the read-only-monitoring posture question is due before the first unattended night. Resolved 2026-09-17: the trigger fired (loop-logs non-empty once the dispatcher went unattended 2026-08-28) and the posture question is answered by the dispatcher's existing controls in harness/dispatcher-ratchets.md (pause file, org-wide open loop-run PR ceiling, per-run MAX_USD fence, rung-gated authority) rather than a separate circuit-breaker layer; monitoring stays read-only. Reopen only on an observed incident those controls did not catch.

column1: dispatcher-stalled
column6: state=$(systemctl --user is-enabled dispatcher-tick.timer 2>/dev/null); rc=$?; case "$state:$rc" in enabled:0|enabled-runtime:0) ;; disabled:1|masked:1|masked-runtime:1) exit 1 ;; *) exit 3 ;; esac; last=$(systemctl --user show dispatcher-tick.timer -p LastTriggerUSec --value 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$last" != n/a ] || exit 3; t=$(date -d "$last" +%s 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$t" ] || exit 3; now=$(date +%s) || exit 3; [ $((now - t)) -gt 2700 ] && exit 0; f=${DISPATCHER_LEDGER_FILE:-$HOME/.claude/logs/dispatcher-ledger.jsonl}; [ -f "$f" ] || exit 1; n=$(jq -rs --argjson cut "$((now - 25200))" '[ group_by(.run_id)[] | sort_by(.ts) | .[-1] | select(.event == "launched" or .event == "claimed") | select((.ts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) < $cut) ] | length' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$n" ] || exit 3; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && exit 0; exit 1
column7: Resolved 2026-10-17: the dispatcher and the owner fleet retired under the merge-and-end rule (dotfiles#1872); sync.sh install removes dispatcher-tick.{service,timer} and its drop-in, so there is no timer to watch. Kept for history: two liveness signals, both required for silence. (1) dispatcher-tick.timer is enabled but its own LastTriggerUSec is older than 3 tick cadences (45 min): the timer stopped firing. (2) The timer is ticking but the ledger's latest row for some run_id is still claimed/launched, with no ended/kept/waste/broken row, and is older than 7 h: a wedged in-flight run. 7 h clears the loop's worst-case wall clock (~2x CLAUDE_LOOP_MAX_MS, 3 h by default); the tick itself keeps exiting 0 during such a run, so OnFailure never fires and reconcile only marks DEAD pids broken. Ledger mtime is deliberately not a signal: an idle tick logs defer:no-eligible-issue and appends nothing (observed 2026-09-17: ticking every 15 min, ledger 5 days old, weekly WARN fired), and a healthy run appends nothing between launched and ended. Known disabled/masked timers are quiet; unreadable timer state, missing or unparseable last-trigger time, and an unreadable ledger are broken, never healthy. A missing ledger is quiet (no runs yet; doctor check 28 owns that at rung >= 1). Read weekly by harness-doctor section 27, so that cadence, not this row, bounds detection latency. No enable/start/stop operation is performed.

column1: ce-upstream-1711
column6: command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; raw=$(gh pr view 1711 -R EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin --json state,author,comments,reviews 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$raw" ] || exit 3; st=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | jq -r .state 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$st" ] || exit 3; [ "$st" = OPEN ] || exit 0; n=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | jq '(.author.login // "") as $a | [ (.comments[]?, .reviews[]?) | (.author.login // "") | select(. != $a and (ascii_downcase | contains("codex-connector") | not)) ] | length' 2>/dev/null) || exit 3; [ -n "$n" ] || exit 3; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && exit 0; exit 1
column7: Upstream contribution EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin#1711 (issue #1710) carries all three dotfiles#826 EXTRACT items. We cannot merge it and must not local-patch around it: the CE local-patch layer was retired 2026-07-01 and FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS would overwrite any local edit. Fires when SOMEONE ELSE responds - a comment or review from a login that is neither the PR author nor the repo's codex-connector bot - or when the PR leaves OPEN. Both exclusions were caught by testing rather than reasoning: their Codex reviewer commented within minutes of opening, and our own reply to that review then fired it again, so a naive any-comment trigger WARNs every week while nothing has happened. The author is read from the PR rather than hardcoded so it survives a re-open by someone else. Two absence cases are deliberately distinguished: no usable gh (absent binary or no auth, as in CI) exits quiet because the check is NOT APPLICABLE on that box, while a usable gh whose query fails exits broken so a real outage never reads as no-news. On fire: update dotfiles#826 and close it if upstream merged or declined.
